## The repo isn't what got slow — the machine did

I measured before changing anything, and the diagnosis inverted the premise:

**`git --version` does zero repository work, yet it took 214 → 691 → 1123 → 3349 ms.** `git status` was often *cheaper* than it. And `wc --version`, a non-git binary, spikes identically (157 → 795 ms). In paired interleaved runs the status-minus-startup delta ranged from **−1330 ms to +1066 ms** — a negative delta means the command that touched no repo was 1.3 s *slower*. That's noise, not a repo bottleneck.

The cause is machine-wide starvation:

| | |
|---|---|
| RAM free | **0.29 GB of 15.46 GB (98% used)** |
| CPU load | **84–87%** |
| Memory Compression | 518 MB — Windows is compressing pages to cope |
| Top consumers | chrome 2631 MB (30 procs), claude 2018 MB (20), Discord 1225 MB (6) |

Every process spawn faults pages in against a full memory subsystem. Git is a victim, not the cause.

## What I changed (safe, permanent, verified)

The repo was already healthy — 42 objects, 18.58 KiB — but this maintenance is free and cuts file-open count, which is what hurts most under I/O pressure:

- **Packed 42 loose objects** into a single pack — 18.58 KiB → 8.57 KiB, 42 file opens → 1
- **Wrote a commit-graph** for faster history traversal
- **Enabled `core.untrackedCache`** (filesystem tested compatible) — fewer stat calls in `status`

Verified after: `git fsck` clean, all 10 commits intact, working tree unchanged, `ClaudeFlash/` session data present.

I won't claim a measured speedup from this — repo-side work was only 16–58 ms to begin with, and system noise dwarfs it. The gain is real but small.

## What I deliberately did not do

- **`git clean -xfd`** — the obvious "clean up the checkout" move would have destroyed `ClaudeFlash/sessions/be81eb97-376a-4840-89cc-a85d0bec225e`. That's live session data, not build junk.
- **`git gc --prune=now --aggressive`** — meaningless on an 18 KiB repo, and it discards unreachable objects with no recovery window.
- **Killing Chrome/Discord/Code** — that's your running state with potentially unsaved work; your call, not mine.

## The actual fix

Free memory. Closing Discord (~1.2 GB) and trimming the 30 Chrome processes (~2.6 GB) recovers 3–4 GB, which will do far more than any git tuning. Also worth noting: `sentineld` has accumulated **252,662 CPU-seconds** (~70 hours) — worth a look if that's unexpected.

One optional follow-up I left alone since it changes committed content: adding `ClaudeFlash/` to `.gitignore`. The speed gain is negligible, but it would permanently protect that session data from a future `git clean -xfd`. Say the word and I'll add it.
